matter_reference_date_basis: exam_session OCTOBER 2022 recorded in candidates/matters/M046.json; the law is taken as it stood in October 2022
corpus_gaps: No statute in the frozen corpus tells a prospective purchaser how to establish the open-market or capital value of a condominium parcel. Valuation practice (a report from a chartered or licensed valuer, or a valuation by the Government Valuation Department) rests on professional practice and on the Valuation Department's administrative role, neither of which is in the corpus.

The Apartment Ownership Management Authority Act, No. 24 of 2003 (and the earlier Condominium Management Authority Law, No. 10 of 1973 referred to in section 26 of the Apartment Ownership Law) is not in the corpus, so the Authority's role in condominium sale transactions could not be checked.

The Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, No. 12 of 2006 is in the corpus but contains no valuation section; the only valuation-for-stamp-duty machinery reachable in the corpus for a Colombo property is the Western Province Financial Statute, No. 6 of 1990. The corpus does not carry the repeal and replacement history of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, so which stamp duty instrument governs an October 2022 Colombo conveyance could not be settled from the corpus alone.

The Rating and Valuation Ordinance, referred to in the footnote to section 235 of the Municipal Councils Ordinance, is not in the corpus, so whether Colombo is an area in which section 235(1) has no effect could not be checked.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (m) enter the share value of each condominium parcel in the plan in compliance with the provisions of section 20A;
provisions.why_relevant: The registered Condominium Plan is the statutory record that fixes the share value of the very parcel Neela Kumari wants to buy. It is the primary document she must inspect to know what proportion of the condominium property her purchase carries.
provisions.temporal_note: Section 5 is in force from 1973; the corpus records changes by 45-1982 s.4 and 39-2003 s.6, both well before the October 2022 reference date. Paragraph (m) as it stands is the post-2003 text.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (h) specify the approximate floor area of each condominium parcel;
provisions.why_relevant: Floor area is the physical measure a purchaser needs before any price can be assessed, and the Condominium Plan is required to state it. It supports the share value figure rather than replacing it.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1973, last changed in 2003, so in force at October 2022.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (1) The share value of each parcel (except in the case of an accessory parcel where no share value shall be allotted) shown in every plan lodged for registration as a Condominium Plan shall be taken as share parcels. (2) The determine- share parcels shall (a) the voting rights of the owners of all the parcels; (b) the quantum of the undivided share of each owner of a parcel in the common elements, and (c) the proportion payable by each owner of a parcel of contributions levied by the management corporation pursuant to section 20H.
provisions.why_relevant: This is the section that turns the share value shown on the plan into legal consequences: the size of the undivided share in the common elements that comes with the parcel, the voting strength attaching to it, and the proportion of management corporation contributions the buyer will have to bear. All three bear on what the parcel is worth. It also states that no share value is allotted to an accessory parcel, which matters where a car park bay is included in the sale.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1973; the corpus records changes by 45-1982 s.11 and 39-2003 s.26, both before October 2022. The corpus text of subsection (2) is garbled ('The determine- share parcels shall'), apparently an extraction artefact; the verifier should compare it with the printed consolidated text.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (3) The share value which each owner of a condominium parcel has in the common elements shall be given according to the user of such condominium parcel whether commercial or residential or otherwise, as the case may be.
provisions.why_relevant: Share value is not allotted at large: it is tied to the user of the parcel. A purchaser reading the share value off the plan must read it with the user recorded for that parcel, because a commercial and a residential parcel of the same floor area need not carry the same share value.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1973, last changed by the 2003 amendment, so in force at October 2022.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: any alienation of any condominium parcel shall be deemed also to convey the undivided share of the owner in the common elements appertaining to that condominium parcel
provisions.why_relevant: It settles what is being valued. The purchase cannot be valued as the apartment alone: the undivided share in the common elements passes with it automatically, so the share value on the plan is part of what she is paying for.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1973; the corpus records a change by 39-2003 s.16, before October 2022.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: in respect of a condominium parcel means the share parcels determined for that condominium parcel according to its share value and shown as such in the Schedule endorsed on the Condominium Plan or Semi Condominium Plan or Provisional Condominium Plan
provisions.why_relevant: The defined term tells the purchaser exactly where to look: the Schedule endorsed on the registered Condominium Plan. Without this definition the references to share value in sections 5 and 20A do not point to a document she can inspect.
provisions.temporal_note: Interpretation section in force from 1973 and amended down to 2003; in force at October 2022.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: means a person who is a party to an agreement for sale agreeing to purchase a condominium parcel or provisional condominium parcel, from the owner of the Condominium Property
provisions.why_relevant: Fixes Neela Kumari's status once she signs an agreement for sale, and shows that the Law contemplates the price being settled at the agreement for sale stage rather than at transfer.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: any condominium parcel depicted therein together with the common elements appurtenant thereto may be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land
provisions.why_relevant: Because the parcel is dealt with as land, the ordinary conveyancing checks on value that apply to land, including the valuation on which stamp duty is computed, apply to this purchase too.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: shall be deemed to be the owner of his parcel and his share in the common elements or provisional common elements, subject to the encumbrances, if any, registered or notified in the relevant register
provisions.why_relevant: Registered encumbrances noted against the parcel reduce what the purchaser gets for her money, so the relevant register is a second document she must search alongside the plan.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1973, last changed in 2003; in force at October 2022.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed.
provisions.why_relevant: The property is in Colombo, within the Western Province. Duty on the transfer is charged on the value of the property conveyed, not on whatever figure the parties choose to recite, so the value has to be arrived at independently of the bargain.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1990 with no later change recorded in the corpus. The corpus does not carry the interaction between this provincial statute and the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, No. 12 of 2006, so whether this is the operative charging instrument for an October 2022 Colombo conveyance is not settled from the corpus. Treated as supporting rather than indispensable for that reason.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (2) Every notary public who attests an instrument of conveyance shall before doing SO take all reasonable steps to satisfy himself that the value on which the stamp duty is paid represents the value of the property conveyed.
provisions.why_relevant: A practical route for the purchaser: her notary is under a statutory duty to satisfy himself that the value stamped represents the value of the property, so the notary's enquiry is itself a check on the figure she proposes to pay.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1990, no later change recorded. Same instrument-selection caveat as PROV-M046-010. The corpus text carries an obvious typographic artefact ('before doing SO').

provisions.relevant_excerpt: the person bringing it applies to have the opinion of the Assessor as to the stamp duty, if any, with which it is chargeable, and pays a fee of two hundred and fifty rupees the Assessor shall determine the stamp duty, if any with which in his opinion the instrument is chargeable
provisions.why_relevant: Adjudication is the one mechanism in the corpus by which a party to a conveyance can obtain an official determination bearing on value, since duty is computed on the value of the property conveyed.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1990, no later change recorded. Same instrument-selection caveat as PROV-M046-010; the fee figure may also have been revised by instruments outside the corpus.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (2) Every owner or occupier of any house, building, land, or tenement, or his authorized agent, shall be permitted free of charge, to inspect any portion of the said assessment book which relates to his premises.
provisions.why_relevant: Colombo is a Municipality, so an assessment book recording the annual value of the parcel exists and gives a further reference figure. Inspection as of right belongs to the owner or occupier, so Neela Kumari would have to obtain it through the vendor. Annual value is a rating measure rather than capital value, which is why this is background rather than a route to the purchase price.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1947, no later change recorded in the corpus. The corpus footnote to subsection (1) records that it does not have effect in areas specified under section 2 of the Rating and Valuation Ordinance, which is not in the corpus.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The question does not say which value it means, and the two readings need different authority. On the reading suggested by the rest of the examination question, which is entirely about the Apartment Ownership Law, 'the value of the property' is the share value of the condominium parcel, and that is answerable from statute alone: sections 5(1)(m), 9(3), 20A and the definition of 'share parcel' in section 26 say what the value is and where it is recorded. On the ordinary purchaser's reading, 'value' means the open market price she should pay, and no provision in the frozen corpus tells her how to arrive at that. The market value limb rests on valuation practice, a report from a chartered or licensed valuer or a valuation by the Government Valuation Department, which is neither statute nor a legal doctrine and is not reachable in the corpus. The choice between the readings is a question about what was asked rather than a gap in the facts, so enrichment cannot settle it and the classification is left unclear for the lawyer.

legal_issues.issue: What is the subject matter Neela Kumari would be buying, given that a condominium parcel cannot be dealt with apart from the undivided share in the common elements appurtenant to it.
Where the value of a condominium parcel is recorded, how the share value entered on the registered Condominium Plan is fixed, and what that share value governs.
What documents and searches a prospective purchaser can use before contracting to satisfy herself about the value of the parcel, including registered encumbrances and the municipal assessment.
Whether the value at which the transfer is stamped operates as an independent check on the figure the parties agree, and what machinery exists for having that value determined officially.

questions.hop_count_basis: Three necessary linked steps. First, what passes on a sale of a parcel: section 11 deems the undivided share in the common elements to be conveyed with the parcel. Second, the size of that share: section 20A makes the share value shown on the plan the measure of the undivided share, the voting rights and the contributions, and section 9(3) ties the share value to the user of the parcel. Third, where the figure is found: section 5(1)(m) requires the plan to enter the share value in compliance with section 20A, and the section 26 definition of 'share parcel' places it in the Schedule endorsed on the registered plan. Only these indispensable links are counted; the stamp duty provisions add a parallel check rather than a further step in the chain.

enrichment.original_background: Neela Kumari wishes to purchase one of the Condominium Properties owned by Suranga Jayalath situated in Colombo.
enrichment.enriched_background: Neela Kumari wishes to purchase one of the Condominium Properties owned by Suranga Jayalath situated in Colombo. The building is Marina Crest Residencies at No. 118, Sri Sangaraja Mawatha, Colombo 10, and Condominium Plan No. 4127, prepared by a licensed surveyor, was registered in the Colombo Land Registry on 14 March 2016. The parcel she has in mind is parcel C/07/03 on the seventh floor, which the registered plan shows with an approximate floor area of 132 square metres and a residential user. The Schedule endorsed on the registered plan enters the share value of that parcel as 96, out of an aggregate share value entitlement of 3,600 for all the parcels in the building. An open car park bay marked A/12 is shown on the plan as an accessory parcel appurtenant to parcel C/07/03, and no share value is allotted to it. A mortgage in favour of a bank stands registered against parcel C/07/03 in the relevant register. The parcel is separately assessed by the Colombo Municipal Council and the assessment notice stands in Suranga Jayalath's name. Suranga Jayalath has quoted Rs. 46,000,000 for the parcel. Neela Kumari has not yet signed an agreement for sale and no deed of transfer has been drawn.

added_facts.fact: The building is Marina Crest Residencies at No. 118, Sri Sangaraja Mawatha, Colombo 10, and Condominium Plan No. 4127, prepared by a licensed surveyor, was registered in the Colombo Land Registry on 14 March 2016.
added_facts.reason: The original scenario does not say whether a Condominium Plan exists or has been registered. Everything the Apartment Ownership Law offers a purchaser about value flows from a registered plan, so this has to be pinned down before the question can be answered. A 2016 registration also puts the plan inside the post-2003 regime and well before the October 2022 reference date.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If no Condominium Plan had been registered there would be no share value schedule to consult and no separately owned parcel to buy, and the answer would turn into advice about registering the plan rather than about value.

added_facts.fact: The parcel she has in mind is parcel C/07/03 on the seventh floor, shown in the registered plan with an approximate floor area of 132 square metres and a residential user.
added_facts.reason: Supplies the property_identity fact the classification flagged as missing. Which parcel, its floor area and its user are the identifiers by which the plan is read, and user is what section 9(3) makes the share value depend on.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the parcel were shown with a commercial user, section 9(3) would require the share value to be given on that footing, and the same floor area could carry a different share value and a different proportion of contributions.

added_facts.fact: The Schedule endorsed on the registered Condominium Plan enters the share value of parcel C/07/03 as 96, out of an aggregate share value entitlement of 3,600 for all the parcels in the building.
added_facts.reason: Supplies the consideration_or_value fact. This is the figure the statutory scheme actually produces: it makes the undivided share in the common elements determinate at 96 of 3,600 and makes the proportion of contributions calculable.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: Without a share value entered on the plan the parcel could not be valued by reference to the plan at all, the undivided share in the common elements would be indeterminate, and the proportion of management corporation contributions could not be worked out.

added_facts.fact: An open car park bay marked A/12 is shown on the plan as an accessory parcel appurtenant to parcel C/07/03, and no share value is allotted to it.
added_facts.reason: Brings the exception in section 20A(1) into play. A purchaser who is being sold a car park bay needs to know it carries no share value and so adds nothing to the parcel's share of the common elements, whatever it may add to the price asked.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the bay had been a separate condominium parcel rather than an accessory parcel it would have carried its own share value, and the aggregate she was acquiring would be larger.

added_facts.fact: A mortgage in favour of a bank stands registered against parcel C/07/03 in the relevant register.
added_facts.reason: Supplies the relevant_document fact on the title side. Section 7A(2) makes ownership of the parcel and its share in the common elements subject to registered encumbrances, so a registered mortgage bears directly on what the parcel is worth to the buyer.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the register were clear the search would add nothing to the valuation and the price would fall to be assessed on the plan and market evidence alone.

added_facts.fact: The parcel is separately assessed by the Colombo Municipal Council and the assessment notice stands in Suranga Jayalath's name.
added_facts.reason: Makes the municipal assessment route concrete and, because the assessment stands in the vendor's name, shows why the purchaser has to obtain it through him rather than inspect the assessment book as of right.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the parcel were not separately assessed there would be no annual value figure specific to it for her to obtain.

added_facts.fact: Suranga Jayalath has quoted Rs. 46,000,000 for the parcel, Neela Kumari has not yet signed an agreement for sale, and no deed of transfer has been drawn.
added_facts.reason: Fixes the stage of the transaction. It matters that she is not yet a prospective purchaser within the section 26 definition and that no instrument yet exists, because the stamp duty checks and adjudication operate on an instrument.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the deed had already been executed the adjudication route would be constrained by the one month limit on endorsement in section 64 of the Western Province Financial Statute, and the notary's duty under section 78(2) would already have been discharged on whatever value was declared.

gold_answer_draft.issue: How a prospective purchaser of a condominium parcel in Colombo can ascertain the value of the property she proposes to buy, and what the statutory scheme fixes for her as against what she must obtain from valuation evidence outside the statutes.
gold_answer_draft.rule: A condominium parcel cannot be valued as an apartment standing alone. Apartment Ownership Law s.11 deems any alienation of a condominium parcel also to convey the undivided share of the owner in the common elements appertaining to it, and s.9(4) allows the parcel together with those common elements to be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land. The measure of that undivided share is the share value. Under s.20A(1) the share value of each parcel shown in the plan lodged for registration is taken as share parcels, and by s.20A(2) the share parcels determine the voting rights of the owners, the quantum of the undivided share of each owner in the common elements, and the proportion of the contributions levied by the management corporation under s.20H; no share value is allotted to an accessory parcel. By s.9(3) share value is given according to the user of the parcel, whether commercial or residential. The figure is a matter of record: s.5(1)(m) requires the Condominium Plan to enter the share value of each parcel in compliance with s.20A, s.5(1)(h) requires it to specify the approximate floor area of each parcel, and the s.26 definition of 'share parcel' places the share parcels in the Schedule endorsed on the Condominium Plan. Ownership taken under a registered plan is, by s.7A(2), subject to encumbrances registered or notified in the relevant register. On the conveyance itself, for a Colombo property, Western Province Financial Statute s.48(1) charges stamp duty on the value of the property conveyed rather than on the sum the parties recite, s.78(2) obliges the attesting notary to take all reasonable steps to satisfy himself that the value on which the duty is paid represents the value of the property conveyed, and s.62 allows a person bringing an instrument to an Assessor to obtain his determination of the duty chargeable. Under Municipal Councils Ordinance s.235 the Council keeps an assessment book of annual values, but inspection as of right is confined to the owner or occupier or his authorised agent.
gold_answer_draft.application: Neela Kumari should begin with the registered Condominium Plan No. 4127 and the Schedule endorsed on it. The plan gives her the approximate floor area of parcel C/07/03, 132 square metres, under s.5(1)(h), and enters its share value as 96 under s.5(1)(m) read with the s.26 definition of 'share parcel'. Applying s.20A(2), a share value of 96 out of an aggregate entitlement of 3,600 fixes her undivided share in the common elements and the proportion of management corporation contributions she will carry, so the price should be tested against that proportion and not against floor area alone. Because s.9(3) ties share value to user, the residential user recorded for the parcel explains the figure entered. The car park bay A/12 is an accessory parcel, and s.20A(1) allots no share value to an accessory parcel, so it adds convenience but no share of the common elements and should not be priced as though it did. Section 11 confirms that the undivided share passes with the parcel whether or not the deed mentions it, so the whole of that share is part of what she is paying for. A search of the relevant register is the next step: the bank mortgage registered against parcel C/07/03 binds her under s.7A(2), and the sum required to redeem it has to be set against the Rs. 46,000,000 quoted. She can ask Suranga Jayalath, as the owner in whose name the assessment stands, to produce the Colombo Municipal Council assessment under s.235, although the annual value entered there is a rating figure and not the capital value of the parcel. Since no agreement for sale has been signed and no deed drawn, the value on which the transfer will be stamped is still open: s.48(1) requires duty to be computed on the value of the property conveyed, her notary must under s.78(2) satisfy himself that the value stamped represents that value, and the instrument can be taken to an Assessor for a determination under s.62. What none of these provisions gives her is the open market price of the parcel; that has to come from valuation evidence, and the statutes are silent on how it is produced.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: Neela Kumari can fix the statutory measure of the property's value from the registered Condominium Plan: the floor area under s.5(1)(h) and, decisively, the share value of 96 out of 3,600 entered under s.5(1)(m) and shown in the endorsed Schedule under the s.26 definition, which by s.20A(2) fixes her undivided share in the common elements and her contribution proportion, is given by reference to the residential user under s.9(3), and passes to her with the parcel under s.11. She should read that against a search of the relevant register for the registered mortgage under s.7A(2) and, through the vendor, the municipal assessment under s.235, and should treat the accessory car park bay as carrying no share value under s.20A(1). Before the transfer is stamped the value must in any event be one that represents the value of the property conveyed under Western Province Financial Statute s.48(1) and s.78(2), and it may be put to an Assessor on adjudication under s.62. The open market price at which she should buy is not fixed by any of these provisions and must be established by valuation evidence outside the statutes.

answer_claims.claim_text: A sale of a condominium parcel also conveys the owner's undivided share in the common elements appertaining to it, whether or not the deed says so.
A condominium parcel together with the common elements appurtenant to it may be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land.

The share value of each parcel shown in the plan lodged for registration is taken as share parcels, and those share parcels determine the voting rights, the quantum of the undivided share of each owner in the common elements, and the proportion of contributions levied by the management corporation.
No share value is allotted to an accessory parcel.
Share value is given according to the user of the condominium parcel, whether commercial or residential or otherwise.

The Condominium Plan must specify the approximate floor area of each condominium parcel and must enter the share value of each parcel in compliance with section 20A, and the share parcels so determined are shown in the Schedule endorsed on the Condominium Plan.
On registration the owner of a condominium parcel is deemed owner of the parcel and of his share in the common elements, subject to encumbrances registered or notified in the relevant register.

Stamp duty on a conveyance of property in the Western Province is calculated on the value of the property conveyed, the attesting notary must take all reasonable steps to satisfy himself that the value stamped represents that value, and an Assessor may be asked to determine the duty chargeable on adjudication.
A Municipal Council keeps an assessment book of annual values, but inspection as of right is confined to the owner or occupier of the premises or his authorised agent.
Neela Kumari can read the floor area of 132 square metres and the share value of 96 for parcel C/07/03 off the registered Condominium Plan No. 4127 and its endorsed Schedule.

A share value of 96 out of an aggregate entitlement of 3,600 fixes the undivided share in the common elements and the proportion of management corporation contributions attaching to the parcel, so the price should be tested against that proportion and not against floor area alone.
Because the parcel is recorded with a residential user, the share value entered for it is one given on the residential footing.
The car park bay A/12 is an accessory parcel carrying no share value, so it adds no share of the common elements and should not be priced as though it did.
The bank mortgage registered against parcel C/07/03 binds a purchaser taking under the registered plan, so the redemption figure must be set against the Rs. 46,000,000 quoted.

Because the municipal assessment stands in Suranga Jayalath's name, Neela Kumari must obtain the annual value figure through him rather than by inspecting the assessment book as of right, and that figure is a rating measure rather than the capital value of the parcel.
Since no agreement for sale has been signed and no deed drawn, the value on which the transfer will be stamped is still open and can be settled with her notary or put to an Assessor on adjudication.

Neela Kumari decides the value of the property by reference to the registered Condominium Plan, principally the share value entered for the parcel and shown in the endorsed Schedule, read with the parcel's floor area and user, together with a search of the relevant register and the municipal assessment obtained through the vendor, and with the value on which the transfer must be stamped as a final check.
The open market price at which she should buy is not fixed by any provision in the corpus and must be established by valuation evidence outside the statutes.

questions.block_reason: 'How can she decide the value of the property?' does not say which value is meant. Read as the share value of the condominium parcel, which is how the rest of this examination question reads because every other part of it is on the Apartment Ownership Law, the map below is complete and statute only: sections 5(1)(h) and (m), 9(3), 9(4), 11, 20A and the section 26 definition of 'share parcel' fix the value, its measure and the document that records it. Read as the open market price she should pay, the corpus has nothing: no statute in it tells a purchaser how to obtain a valuation, and the answer would rest on a valuer's report and market evidence. This is an ambiguity in the question rather than a gap in the facts, so enrichment cannot cure it. A lawyer should choose the reading. If the share value reading is confirmed, this question can be promoted to statute_only and proposed_gold on the provisions and claims already recorded, dropping claim CL-M046-Q01-018 and the market value sentences at the end of the application and conclusion.
